sources.citation: SIL Language & Culture Archives, language listing for Jibu [jib] (Internet Archive copy 2015-09-19): 11 items (Van Dyken 1974, Bradley 1971, 'Towards readable writing', primers, Jibu-Hausa-English wordlist 1974, literacy books, NT portions 1993); no separate phonology ms listed.
Glottolog 5.x languoid record jibu1239 and reference records 81866 (Van Dyken 1974, listed by Glottolog as a phonology) and 19100 (Bradley 1971).
sources.note: Bibliographic only; 2 descriptive refs in total.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Jibu language' (wikitext, downloaded 2026-09-17): three tones H/M/L, 18 consonants, 9 vowels, citing Bradley 1971:15 and the Priest/Blench dictionary.

Blench, Roger. 2020. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV (2019). Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. Entry 226 Jukun cluster, **Jibu (Gashaka LGA; refs: 'Phonology: Van Dyken (1974); Grammars: Bradley (1971)').
sources.note: Nothing; confirms no other phonological description of Jibu is known.

sources.citation: Priest, Perry [comp.], ed. Roger Blench. n.d. [2006]. Jibu Dictionary. Circulation draft. 41 pp. (Jibu-PoS-English-Hausa wordlist posted on rogerblench.info)
sources.note: Nothing. Bare tone-marked wordlist (acute=H, grave=L, unmarked=M; e.g. kab / káb / kàb, p.18), no introduction or prose; the words stress/accent/tone/syllable do not occur.

sources.citation: Welmers, William E. 1968. Jukun of Wukari and Jukun of Takum. (Occasional Publication 16.) Ibadan: Institute of African Studies.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.82.9.50.9.30 (16); Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8301.W4)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number L.SOC.82.9.50.9.30 (16); Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL8301 .W4
sources.note: Concerns Wapan and Diyi (Takum) only; Jibu of Serti is not mentioned (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing). Its stress remark (1.9.4, non-phonemic stress tied to rising tones) does not apply to jibu1239.

sources.citation: Meek, C. K. 1931. A Sudanese Kingdom: an ethnographical study of the Jukun-speaking peoples of Nigeria. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner.
sources.note: Nothing. pp.1-2 'Linguistics' lists Jibu as one of six Jukun dialects with a comparative root table and a note on pronominal prefix/suffix; no phonology; 'stress'/'accent' only in non-linguistic senses.
